newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria says Israel bringing region to brink of war.
newsitem.headline: Syria says Israel bringing region to brink of war.

text.p: Syria has accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of bringing the region to the brink of war by refusing to make peace with Damascus and building settlements in occupied Arab lands.

"The Israeli government led by Netanyahu refuses to make peace, rejects (U.N.) resolutions 242 and 338, and opposes the land-for-peace formula. It wants to put the region on the verge of a new war...," Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara said.
Shara's remarks to television networks in Germany, where he is paying an official visit, were published by official Syrian newspapers on Wednesday.
The papers quoted him as saying that Netanyahu's plans to build 6,500 housing units in Arab East Jerusalem would not succeed.

"But he might succeed in escalating tension in the region and in dragging Arabs into a confrontation that he would be responsible for. The world realises that Netanyahu does not want peace but is putting the region on the verge of new wars," Shara said.

He reiterated Syria's view that peace talks between Israel and Damascus, which broke off a year ago, could not be resumed if Netanyahu did not accept the outcome of negotiations with the former Labour-led Israeli government.

Syria says the former Israeli government, which was defeated by Netanyahu in elections last May, had agreed during talks with Damascus to withdraw fully from the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967.
Israel began work on Tuesday at the site of the planned Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem with bulldozers ploughing up the hill of Jabal Abu Ghneim, called Har Homa by Israel.
The official Syrian daily al-Baath said on Wednesday that Palestinians who decided first to confront the plans peacefully would now turn to violence to stop the building.
The Tishreen daily compared Netanyahu's policies with those of Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler, "who invaded Europe, destroyed human beings, expelled people and seized their properties."
The English-language daily Syria Times urged the United States, as a sponsor of Arab-Israeli peace talks, to step in to rescue the faltering Middle East peace process.

"A strong, firm response from Washington, showing the administration of President Bill Clinton in its second term in office is committed to keep the peace talks on track, is needed urgently and vehemently," Syria Times said.
Fayez al-Sayegh, director-general of the official Syrian news agency Sana, said in a comment published by al-Thawra daily that Arabs should unite to stop Israel's building plans.

"If the United States is not giving a serious initiative it is better for Arabs themselves to adopt firm and serious actions to respond to the catastrophe which is facing peace and the city of Jerusalem," Sayegh said.
